notes: Full description: pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs RevocationChecker trait, check_revocation() at line 194. The #[must_use] attribute is on the trait method. In Rust, #[must_use] on a trait method is respected by the compiler for direct calls, but the real enforcement here is that Result<()> is already #[must_use] as a type. The annotation is redundant but harmless. The actual important issue: check_revocation_against_anchor() has a DEFAULT IMPLEMENTATION that returns Ok(()) silently. The doc comment at lines 162-169 explicitly warns 'Implementors that want full-chain revocation coverage MUST also override check_revocation_against_anchor. The default implementation skips the check silently; forgetting to override it will leave the anchor-issued certificate unchecked with no compile error or runtime warning.' This is a security-relevant silent skip that cannot be enforced at compile time. There is no mechanism (marker trait, type-state, etc.) to require implementors to override this method. Fix: Consider a two-trait design where RevocationChecker only handles cert-to-cert and a separate FullRevocationChecker requires the anchor case, or add a runtime assertion option. Priority: P2 (security design gap — easy to silently miss anchor revocation).
title: FINDING: check_revocation_against_anchor default is silent Ok() with no enforcement
